text:
I added `hashtags(text)` to `src/shop/core.py`, with tests in `tests/test_hashtags.py`. All 11 tests pass.

- **Behaviour:** Matches the spec: a `#` at the start of the text or after whitespace, followed by one or more `\w` characters. Results are lowercased, without the `#`, deduplicated case-insensitively, and kept in order of first appearance.
- **Tests:** Cover basic extraction, empty input, dedup and ordering, start-of-text, whitespace variants, `a#b` being ignored, digits and underscores, lone `#` and `##`, punctuation, and `#abc#def`.
- **CHANGELOG:** Added an entry under Unreleased, referencing PAY-4103.

Choices you may want to change:
- **Unicode letters:** I used Python's `\w`, so non-ASCII letters such as `#café` count as hashtags. If you want ASCII-only, I can switch to `[A-Za-z0-9_]`.
- **Export:** `src/shop/__init__.py` is empty, and so is the existing `total`, so I did not export `hashtags` from the package. Import it as `from shop.core import hashtags`.
- **Test dependency:** pytest wasn't installed on this machine, so I installed it in a venv at `/tmp/shop-venv-pytest`, outside the repo. The repo has no requirements file, so nothing was added to it.

The repo isn't a git repository, so I didn't commit anything.
prompt: Add a new feature called hashtags to this package (ticket PAY-4103). It should provide hashtags(text), returning the unique hashtags in order of first appearance, lowercase and without the '#'. A hashtag is a '#' followed by one or more letters, digits or underscores, and the '#' must be at the start of the text or right after whitespace (so 'a#b' has none). Compare case-insensitively when deciding uniqueness. Also add tests.
